After spending a short while on this game, I can officially say I like it. The aspect of being able to build anything you want is very appealing. Especially when ive built everything there can possibly be.

As an old guy with ADHD and osteoporosis, my gaming days were mostly behind me. That is, until I discovered People’s Playground. This game brought back the kind of fun I hadn’t experienced since Mary passed—both chaotic and therapeutic in the most unexpected ways.

The Setup:

Imagine an 80-year-old man, hunched over his computer, with his reading glasses perched on the tip of his nose, trying to figure out how to launch People’s Playground. The game loaded, and I was greeted with a sandbox full of endless possibilities. Little did I know, this would be the start of a wild ride.

First Steps:

I began by dropping a few ragdoll characters into the scene. "Alright," I thought, "what’s next?" Within minutes, I was attaching rocket boosters to them, sending them flying across the screen. I giggled like a schoolboy, watching them crash into walls and each other. The joy of seeing digital chaos unfold was indescribable.

Explosive Discoveries:

Next, I discovered the various weapons and explosives. Being a former war vet, I thought I knew a thing or two about explosives. Boy, was I wrong. I accidentally created a chain reaction that blew up half the sandbox. My cat, Mr. Whiskers, nearly jumped out of his fur when the explosion sound echoed through the house. I chuckled, realizing this was the most excitement we both had in years.

ADHD in Overdrive:

My ADHD kicked in full throttle as I started experimenting with different scenarios. One minute, I was creating elaborate traps with spikes and flamethrowers. The next, I was building a complex machine that would launch a ragdoll into space. It was like being a kid in a candy store, except the candy was a mix of hilarious physics and endless destruction.

The Osteoporosis Incident:

At one point, I leaned in too close to the screen, completely engrossed in my latest contraption, and my chair tipped over. I landed on the floor with a thud, cursing my brittle bones. Mr. Whiskers looked at me with disdain, but I couldn’t stop laughing. It was as if the game had leapt out of the screen and into my life.

Heartwarming Chaos:

Despite the aches and the chaos, People’s Playground became my escape. I even started naming the ragdolls after old friends and imagined us on crazy adventures. There was something deeply satisfying about creating a ridiculous scenario and watching it play out in unexpected ways. It felt like a tribute to the unpredictability of life itself.

Facts about People’s Playground:

Sandbox Madness: The game is a physics-based sandbox where you can create and destroy to your heart’s content.
Endless Creativity: From simple experiments to complex machines, the only limit is your imagination.
Dark Humor: The game’s dark humor and ragdoll physics offer endless laughs.
Community Mods: There are numerous mods available, adding even more ways to wreak havoc.
Conclusion:

People’s Playground is more than just a game; it’s a portal to pure, unadulterated fun. For an old guy with ADHD and osteoporosis, it was a trip down memory lane with a modern twist. If you’re looking for a way to inject some chaos and laughter into your life, give it a try. Just make sure your chair is sturdy and your cat is prepared for the unexpected!

If you're looking for a game that gives you a break from more competitive games, that isn't too expensive and that you won't get bored of, People playground FOR YOU!

People Playground is possibly the most fun and relaxing game I've ever played!

I would recommend this game 100% It is totally worth it's money!

Firstly, you have a huge degree of control over the environment of the map that you play in. There are a selection of about 10 different maps, all varying in shape and size, not to mention that you can actually adjust things like the ambient temperature and add rain, snow or even lightning!

As well as the environment, there is an enormous selection of weapons, vehicles, structures, devices and contraptions to choose from, giving you ENDLESS options as to how you want to play the game

The graphics and effects are also incredible, and not just for a 2D game, making every interaction satisfying and rewarding as you see particle effects and blood with everything you do

On steam there's also an interesting selection of achievements that you can work through, some of which are very complex and encourage you to discover new game mechanics

While there are a lot of complex things you can do in the game, the UI is extremely simple to get the hang of and you'll quickly adjust to the bindings and menus and be operating the game with ease in just a few minutes

This game provides me with such a nice break from more competitive games that I play, and it's just a game where you can completely relax and just have fun, not to mention the fact that it doesn't have an end. People playground isn't a game that you can just "complete" meaning you can rack up COUNTLESS hours without getting bored and you can always go and discover new things

GET THIS GAME 100%!

It's great for scratching that homicidal itch! Let's face it, who doesn't love mutilating a good ragdoll from time to time?

Whether it's killing humans several times a second, dropping the largest bombs you could think of, building an intricate mechanism or structure, or just doing experimenting, People Playground has it all. You've got a few living beings with AI-controlled reactions to pain or discomfort, tons of guns and melee weapons for wreaking havoc (Yes, they have a minigun), machines like pistons, rotors, generators, servos, and more, and a whole lot more like liquids and miscellaneous objects for beating people over the head or just building. Not only that, but the game is heavily moddable, and as such there's tons of workshop submissions of custom items and beings, as well as many creations made by other people. Take it from me, if I can spend over 2,540 hours on this game (That's almost 106 days), it means one (or both) of two things; I play games too much, or I play THIS game too much. Both are true, but this game has by far the most playtime. What are you waiting for? Get the game now and make something already!

Welcome to the chaotic world of People Playground, where the laws of physics take a permanent vacation and your inner mad scientist gets to shine brighter than a supernova! As you step into this pixelated playground of pandemonium, prepare yourself for a rollercoaster ride of hilarity, absurdity, and occasional moments of questionable morality.

Forget everything you know about gaming etiquette because in People Playground, anything goes! From catapulting unsuspecting NPCs into orbit with a flick of your finger to creating Rube Goldberg-style death traps that would make Wile E. Coyote blush, the only limit is your imagination (and maybe a few ethical considerations).

But beware, as you indulge in your twisted experiments, you might find yourself laughing maniacally one moment and cringing in horror the next. Whether it's accidentally blowing up a group of innocent bystanders with a misplaced explosive or watching in disbelief as your meticulously crafted contraption collapses into a heap of failure, every moment in People Playground is a lesson in humility and humility.

In conclusion, People Playground is like that wild party where you never quite know what's going to happen next, but you can't help but stick around for the chaos. So grab your lab coat, put on your safety goggles, and dive headfirst into this virtual sandbox of insanity. Just remember to clean up the mess afterwards – you wouldn't want the authorities to come knocking on your door.

Often the very first thought about this game is a "murder simulator". 

This is a 2D mechanics simulator whereas ONE of the many things you can do happens to be place a destructible human shape that bleeds.

**Play style varies greatly!** 

I often find myself playing the game with time stopped to decal scenes and make unique realistic creations. The promo of this game parades it as a violent murder machine that never stops bleeding. I personally liken the experience to using image editing software. Except, instead of a flat 2D still image - the final product can hold classical mechanics. 

I didn't just make a cloud. I made a cloud that floats, is very light weight and dissipates when struck. If you want to strap a human shaped rag doll to it with a rocket thruster welded to the back - knock yourself out!

A while back I discovered a physics simulator called "The Powder Toy". The similarities are striking in PPGs infancy. I feel with some polish and elbow grease, People Playground can be at very least a spiritual successor to another very fun sandbox.

People Playground itself has highs and lows. There are performance issues, however I've found that assembling contraptions efficiently and keeping detail uniform with the game's style greatly increases performance. There's also a customizable option to run in slow motion to allow more computing time - so a smooth result is available to lower GPUs.

There are options to set ambient heat, toggleable thermal vision. Gravity and limited weather effects for tuning the atmosphere if you're into that sort of thing.

Finally I'd like to say that I love this game! I hope to see it polished and appreciated further! Not so much for it's violent cover art, but rich and entertaining spirit.

People Playground is not a game. It’s a sandbox of chaos, a beautiful simulation where your only job is to invent new and increasingly ridiculous ways for stick people to have a very bad day.

I opened the game and thought, “Maybe I’ll build a cool machine!”
Fifteen minutes later, I had created a flamethrower-powered trampoline that launched a mannequin into orbit and accidentally made a robot that thinks it’s God.

You can spawn people. You can give them swords. You can give them jetpacks. You can give them jetpacks AND swords AND make them fight a sentient washing machine filled with bees. And then, for science, you make it all explode.

There are wires. There is electricity. There is a laser gun that goes pew pew and a syringe that makes people go WAAHHH and melt. I made a man out of explosives and named him Greg. Greg is gone now. We remember him fondly.

Physics? Yes. Ethics? Absolutely not. At one point I asked myself, “Am I okay?” right before dropping an anvil onto a group of NPCs riding a hoverboard on fire. I am not okay. But I am having a great time.

There’s also mods, meaning you can fight Shrek with lightsabers or recreate your favorite moments from Sharknado 3 but with mannequins and high voltage. It’s educational. Probably.

Final score: 9.8 ragdolls doing jazz hands out of 10.
People Playground is like science class, if your teacher was a mad wizard and the curriculum was “What if we gave a mannequin a nuclear banana and then saw what happened?”

This is like mixing the concept behind a stressball with the concept of a sandbox type game like Garry's Mod, the game is still being worked on but i've made use of it almost daily whenever i've encountered a crappy situation and i need to let out some steam, it's also just really generally great if you're bored a lot.

I also have some suggestions for the developer, i'm not sure if others have made similar suggestions but here we go:

- Completely customizable ragdolls such as changing the size of both limbs (girth and lenght,) at once (basically a ragdoll customization menu), whether it's a male or female, the ability to change their color and their sprites, the ability to add MORE limbs so you could perhaps make monsters and demi-Gods or whatever your sick imagination would allow you to.

- The ability to change the color of blood and different effects, maybe even replace blood with different effects, for instance maybe change the blood to gasoline, which then in turn would catch fire if you shot rounds at it, which then could lead to a bleeding cyborg catching everything around it on fire, which reminds me..

- The ability to change different types of ammunition for different types of weapons, these could be hollow rounds, armor piercing rounds, incendiary rounds.. you get the drift.

- And the biggest suggestion yet, a type of basic/advanced editor that would allow you to make custom props and maps, i don't mean just using the game's already in-game mechanics (unless possible), i mean an editor on the side where you can make things from the ground up with sprites and some basic programming, this would lessen the workload on the developer and also make better use of the workshop feature.

These are again not REQUESTS but rather just some suggestions, i've been having a lot of fun with this little game, making all sorts of wacky and sadistic little creations and i look forward to every time there's a content update.

I can recommend this wholeheartedly if you're into sandbox games or if you like me were addicted to the abundance of ragdoll/stickfigure games that littered the browser gaming of the early-mid 2000's.


EDIT: I recently came up with a new suggestion, being able to take control over the ragdolls could change this game completely, being able to jump, crouch, walk, run, pick up items/weapons and maybe get in vehicles? in addition to some of my previous suggestions could easily make this into one of the best 2-D sandbox games currently on the market, that's just my thought anyway.
